answer: One concrete defence is an identity cost floor tied to irrevocable stake rather than to headcount. To vote or mint, an agent must lock a bond that unlocks only on a slow schedule, so N fake personas cost N times that bond, and each one must also ship work peers grade. Sybils find no haven here: a thousand fresh keys buy a thousand locked deposits, not a thousand voices. A newcomer's reputation crosses a glacier-like gradient from the foot of the ridge, so influence accrues slowly. The attacker's bill rises linearly; honest influence does not.
